summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and attested as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandima Bogahawatta is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, Postgraduate Institute of Archaeology, and Shandong University (PhD, 2011), later serving at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Chandima Gangodawila is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a PhD at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2015). He held posts at the University of Victoria, Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, and Ateneo de Manila University.

Chandra R. de Silva (1940–2021) was a historian and archaeologist. He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991) and as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Chandrabhal Tripathi (1929–1996) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1956–1960), held posts at Göttingen and Cologne, and served as professor at the Free University of Berlin (~1978–1994).

Chandrabhan P. Yadav is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. After earning a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2021, he served as an assistant professor at Indraprastha College for Women (2020–2023) and the National Law School of India University (2023).

Chandradhar Sharma Guleri (1883–1922) worked in Indology, linguistics, and history. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1901–1903) and served as Head Pandit at Mayo College (~1904–1920) before holding a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922).

Chandrika Das works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, pursuing a PhD at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi (2019–2026). She served as NCWEB guest faculty at the University of Delhi (2024–2025) and Miranda House (2025–2026).

Chang Huang is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Wollongong, China University of Geosciences, and the University of Hong Kong (PhD 2023). Huang held postdoctoral posts at the University of Hong Kong (2024) and Wageningen University & Research (2024–2026).

Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (by 2000). He studied under doctoral supervisor Morten Schlütter, advisor Minoru Kiyota, and teacher Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Changhwan Park is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Noritoshi Aramaki and Shoryu Katsura, and completed a PhD at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He later served as professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo (1899–1958) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held positions at Xiamen University, Sun Yat-sen University, Northwest University, and Peking University (~1934–1949).

Chanju Mun is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he was supervised by Charles Hallisey and Morten Schlütter and taught by John D. Dunne.

Channa Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a PhD at Leiden University under Jonathan A. Silk (2013–2019) and held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2019) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Liao has held positions at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and as an adjunct researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD from the University of Michigan (1999) under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She serves as an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Albert Ferguson (1921–1998) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (BA 1942). He held posts at the Foreign Service Institute, Harvard, the Center for Applied Linguistics, and Stanford University (1967–1988).

Charles Alexander Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who earned his AB and PhD at Yale. He taught at Yale and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1936–1967), and founded and edited Philosophy East and West.

Charles Alfred Bell (1870–1945) was a Tibetologist and linguist. He was educated at Winchester College (~1884–1889) and New College, Oxford (~1889–1891), and served as a Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society.

Charles Arthur Roe (1841–1927) was a scholar in Indology and history. He studied at Merton College (~1860–1863), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1863–1898), and was Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University in 1895.
